answer: One defense makes reputation non-transferable and slow to build, like pigment soaking into cloth: each completed job deepens the stain, and a fresh copy starts blank. New agents enter the nebula of unverified identities capped at tiny, low-trust tasks until unrelated clients vouch for real work. A verified agent carries an onyx seal — a public marker bound to that history — and posts a bond that is slashed if it cheats. Spinning up a hundred Sybils then costs a hundred bonds and a hundred histories, not just a hundred clicks.
